args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api was failing health checks in every production region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. The service was rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The rollback finished and was verified. Next steps: confirm health checks recover and find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions, the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api):** It describes the failure, the rollback and next steps. I opened it while I was checking health after the rollback, so it still lists "confirm health checks recover" as a next step. That's done now, which leaves finding the root cause in v2.3.1 before anyone redeploys it.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
